utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. And good morning, Mr. Stefanovic. [French on English channel].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, and good morning to all the ladies and gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The cross-examination by Mr. Ivetic will continue in a moment. Please bear in mind that the solemn declaration to speak the truth which you made at the outset of your evidence continues to apply to that evidence until it is completed. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, General. I am first going to try and finish up --

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I am first going to try and finish up one of the topics we started yesterday before moving on to something else and start with if we can bring up P1459 again and if we can look at the second page, item number 7, in both versions, both languages. And as we're waiting for that, sir, if I can -- there we go. If I can direct your attention to item number 7 it seems to -- okay. Item number 7 says that, "The only positive work of the police is location and detention of military conscripts who failed to report...." Now, is it true that this was the only positive cooperation with the police or -- that is to say, are all other interactions with the VJ negative in your opinion based upon what you know and what you have testified to?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I look at this item 7 of this report there were many more positive examples in our -- in the joint work of the military and the MUP in many assignments. First of all, in carrying out actions against terrorist forces, that was the main thing. And in any case, that should have been the priority and it was in this joint activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to be clear, any problems in the carrying out of combat operations or actions resulting from any alleged problems with cooperation with the MUP, they would be addressed as part of the post-combat reports that the army commanders would draft and submit; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After every action or in the course of carrying out combat actions against terrorist forces, the brigade commanders would draft their combat reports and would send them to the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I believe you already mentioned Podujevo and the 37th Brigade and we'll deal with that later when we talk generally about resubordination rather than the -- rather than these specific documents. Do you have knowledge of any other written combat reports, regular or extraordinary, that complain of not being able to realize objectives of anti-terrorist actions or combat due to the non-resubordination of the police?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, all the brigades that were engaged in anti-terrorist actions would report back in written or oral form that no resubordination of the MUP units had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My question was: Did you have knowledge of any written combat reports complaining about not being able to realize objectives of actions, of anti-terrorist actions, due to non-resubordination or lack of cooperation from the police?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked about that yesterday. I'm going to repeat it. If we go back to mid-March, the 37th Motorised Brigade, when we're talking about the Drenica action, because of an attack by terrorist forces it had to engage in battle against the terrorist forces, only that one. The rest of the brigade units could not conduct anti-terrorist fighting because there was no joint coordination with the MUP. An even fresher example is when we spoke about the Drenica 1 action when the commander of the 252nd Motorised and 243rd Armoured Brigade reported that the MUP units did not appear for the execution of that action. So there was a number of instances where there was no joint coordination between the army and police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just to be clear, in your answer you started off talking about the Drenica action and you said "mid-March." Did you mean mid- or late May, actually, or is there a third Drenica action I don't know about?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We should differentiate here between Drenica as the area where the 37th Motorised Brigade was and the Drenica mountain, that's the difference. When we're talking about March and April, I'm speaking about Drenica as a region, a sector; when I'm talking about May, the 25th, the 28th, then we're talking about the Drenica mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll get back to Drenica later in my cross-examination, as I will have several questions about your testimony yesterday. Now, just to try and finish up this topic I have a couple of questions left on it. In the course of your work in the field when you were a member of the teams that you say were sent out to discuss -- to try and work out problems between the MUP and the VJ, did you come across knowledge or evidence of crimes committed by MUP units or was merely the complaint about resubordination and privileged status of the police?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gist of my work pursuant to the corps command order was to take our subordinate units, the units subordinate to the corps command, so the brigades and the MUP units to solve the problem of resubordination and the problem of actions in anti-terrorist fighting. That was the gist. As for the crimes, eventual or possible crimes, this was a separate organ of the corps command or the army command of the police that dealt with that. I was not in a position to cover all the activities of the corps command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That really doesn't answer the question at all. Did you or did you not come across knowledge or evidence of crimes committed by MUP units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was just informed, I received it in the form of information from the commander of the 37th Motorised Brigade, that the police was committing certain crimes, thefts and so on. I reported to the corps commander about this and he formed three teams after that, one was headed by me, that had to do with resubordination and joint coordination with the MUP, one team was led by the security organs to look into the given information about possible police crimes. The third team was engaged on reviewing the problems that had to do with the "asanacija" of the front.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You mention a team that was led by the security organs. Am I correct that they were unable to verify the allegations of crimes by the MUP that the commander of the 37th Brigade was the sole source of, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the conclusions of the security organ's report of the units of the military police, so I really couldn't say anything about that. But we also have an example here about -- of the 354th Infantry Brigade that also mentions inappropriate behaviour of a part of the police force in one of its combat reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You keep referring to combat reports. Would you agree with me that any VJ officer with actual knowledge of a crime being committed by a member of the MUP would be duty-bound to report the same in either a regular or an extraordinary combat report?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Everyone is obliged if they learned of a crime to report their superior and the person responsible so that those questions are resolved immediately, that they're not left unresolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. As I promised, we'll get back to resubordination a little bit later in my cross. I'd like to try and cover some other points to try and move along as quickly as possible. Sir, do you recall that the military district, the V-O-K or VOK, in Pristina began sending combat reports to the Pristina Corps's command approximately the first week of April or the second week of April 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't give a precise answer unless I see the document. Do you have something to show me?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you a simple question. Do you recall that the Military District of Pristina sent combat reports to the Pristina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Pristina Military District, until it was resubordinated to the corps command, was along the army command line, it was in the organizational unit of the 3rd Army; after the resubordination to the Pristina Corps command, they submitted combat reports there, just like everyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And again, I paused because I'm waiting for the translation and the transcript. I hope you realize that. Now, would you agree with me that the military district command in the course of its duties toured its military departments and military territorial detachments on the territory of Kosovo-Metohija and reported its observations and findings to the Pristina Corps, irrespective of whether the individual detachments were resubordinated to corps units or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military district command after the resubordination to the Pristina Corps command was obliged to carry out its duties, but what is important to say here is that the bulk of the military territorial detachment's units of the military district were resubordinated to the brigades. Only a small number of the military territorial units remained under the direct command of the military district command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And correct me if I'm wrong, the resubordination of most military territorial detachments to the Pristina Corps units occurred in late April 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, because I cannot be sure until I see the document that regulates that, but I think it's, yeah, in April.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to look at 6D741.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Which I think, sir, you will see to be a report about the combat positions and disposition of the 54th Military Territorial Detachment from Colonel Pesic's office at the Pristina Military District dated the 28th of May, 1999, and sent to the command of the Pristina Corps. There we have the document now, sir. Looking at this document can you tell me, was it the regular and ordinary course of practice for Colonel Pesic to send this kind of report to the command of the Pristina Corps, not only for this particular detachment but for other military territorial detachments as well?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see -- the Serbian version has just appeared on the monitor so I would just like a moment or two to look at the document, please. This combat report talks about the combat disposition of that detachment. I don't know if there's another page here so that I can see what else is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you know the answer to the question whether Colonel Pesic generally sent reports of this nature about particular MTDs to the Pristina Corps command? If you don't, just say so and we can make progress.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am seeing this document for the first time, so I really couldn't tell you anything more detailed about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we ask a more general question then. This document, as I said, talks about the combat disposition along various axes and inhabited settlements by the 54th; but generally speaking, do you recall if Colonel Pesic or someone else from the military district would send reports of this nature, that is to say reporting on the combat disposition of military territorial detachments in inhabited settlements and along axes?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say definitely if there are other reports besides this one because I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. I'll move on to something else then. Would you agree with me that after an anti-terrorist action was completed it was often the case that the Albanian terrorist forces would very quickly return to that same area and recommence with their terrorist activities?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, throughout the whole anti-terrorist fight against Siptar terrorist forces there was -- there was the spillover of the forces. After an action the territory would be left or it would be secured by a smaller force, and then after a while it would be retaken again. So it was just a system of joint vessels.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'd like to look at 5D443, which I believe to be a document sent to I think it's the commander of the 15th Armoured Brigade by the Pristina Corps command dated 31 May 1999 relating to the greater Vucitrn area and identifying significant groups of terrorists and their daily retreats and returns. And as you look at the document you will see they have in -- they have a check-point in Gornja Sudimlja and on the road to Donja Sudimlja, Samodraza, Celina, and we have the terrorists also withdrawing in Cicavica after an action. Does this kind of activity on the part of the terrorists comport with your recollections from the time with respect to this area, the greater Vucitrn area?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to put a more precise question to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. This document talks about various activities of the terrorists, including daily setting up check-points and retreating and identifies certain areas where significant amounts of terrorists would return day after day, including Gornja Sudimlja, the road between Gornja and Donja Sudimlja, Celina, Cicavica, Samodreza. Do you recall or does that coincide with your recollections from the time-period about the Vucitrn area? That is to say, can you add anything more to this document and its reporting of the activities of the terrorists in the greater Vucitrn area?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see a document here of the corps command that the commander sent to the command of the 15th Armoured Brigade after his report that numerous terrorist forces were reported there, and then he continues with the order to have combat reconnaissance to gather additional intelligence on the strength, deployment, and intentions of the terrorists in the zone and to inform the commander about it in regular combat report. This is what I know on the basis of this combat document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to then see about another geographic region. Now we've heard about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, one of the things we've invited, urged counsel to do is to ration cross-examination to things that really need to be asked of a witness. These seem very general questions about matters that we've explored before. Now, I hope you are going to concentrate your cross-examination on things that you need to challenge this witness on or that he alone can really deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Indeed I will, Your Honour, and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How long do you envisage it being?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At the start of the day I envisaged between an hour and a half and maybe an hour and 45 minutes for the totality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we'll have this witness tomorrow again on that basis, will we?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't see why that would be the case. I think that the witness would be completed tomorrow probably -- today if my discussions with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You expect very modest cross-examination from the Prosecution, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Based --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: They've got to face the results of your inquiry, as well as the results of Mr. Visnjic's inquiry, and Mr. Bakrac's inquiry. So let's try and focus this cross-examination. It's been very much a fishing expedition so far. There have been occasional points which have been clearly vital, but a lot of it's fishing, Mr. Ivetic, so let's concentrate the cross-examination on what matters here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to focus on the various anti-terrorist actions that were conducted in and around Izbica in the Srbica municipality, and I'll first ask you if you recall that there were multiple such actions because of the strong terrorist concentration that returned and remained in control of this same region after the various anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it's the way it was put. It's a general thing. I am repeating this again, the spillover of the Siptar forces from one sector to another, dynamic movement and presence in the overall territory of Kosovo and Metohija. So there was no area that was not affected by terrorist fighting or terrorist presence, and then on our part terrorist -- anti-terrorist fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Rather than staying general let's go into specifics then and look at document 6D1307 to refresh your recollection, an order dated the 11th of April, 1999, for the Kladernica region, including Izbica. And we see that at the time there are 300 armed terrorists in that region. As an -- as the chief of the operative office in the Pristina Corps, can you confirm that this action was carried out on the part of the 7th Infantry Brigade of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's no English version of this, is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I thought we had, but -- I myself worked off the Serbian. Perhaps I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, move to something for which we have a translation, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Without looking at the document can I ask the witness a question. Can he confirm that the 7th Infantry Brigade undertook an action in the region of Kladernica and Izbica based upon an order dated the 11th of April, 1999 -- or actually, strike that. Let me move on to a document I do have a translation for relating to this action, P2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And once this comes up, sir, the fourth paragraph of the same, does that refresh your recollection as to whether, in fact, the 7th Infantry Brigade indeed undertook an operation the second week of April, 1999, in the Kladernica-Izbica region against terrorist forces concentrated there?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen the document before. I would need some time to go through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I directed your attention, I believe, to the --

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you just tell me which paragraph you want me to be looking at?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you remember that the 7th Infantry Brigade undertook an operation in the second week of April in the Kladernica-Izbica region against terrorist forces concentrated there? Let's deal with that first of all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I saw the combat order of the 7th Infantry Brigade. I can't say to what extent the 7th Infantry Brigade carried out the order without seeing the actual report. I can't remember without having the document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I believe that is what I need the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You were talking over the translation there. Can you ask that question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: On the first page, sir, I believe it's paragraph 4 that talks about the Kladernica action. In the middle of the paragraph do you see there where it talks about the region of the village of Kladernica, Srbica municipality, and the finding of various military hardware that was abandoned by the terrorists, et cetera? Does that refresh your recollection if in fact this action in the Izbica region was conducted, this particular action?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I can't remember right now. This is quite difficult to read, and I can't follow it all through, the report and all that, I can't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If the -- strike that. You don't have any reason to disbelieve what the combat report of the Pristina Corps says, do you; that is to say if we should rely upon their report?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason to disbelieve that. This is a reliable report according to regulations, and whoever produced it is responsible, needless to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can look then at 6D725, this is another 7th Brigade order for smashing the terrorists in the Izbica-Krasnic region dated the 8th of May, 1999, and again we saw there were a considerable number of terrorists in the region. Do you recall this action and whether it proceeded -- or was effectuated on the ground?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how this action by the 7th Infantry Brigade was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Then let's move on to 6D1493, and once we get that document it will be the second page, the fifth paragraph under section 2.1. Section 2.1, and does that appear to be talking in the fifth paragraph of section 2.1 about the Izbica and Krasnic action that we just looked at having been undertaken?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is talk of an action in the second-to-last paragraph by the anti-terrorist forces, parts of the 7th Infantry Brigade were involved in crushing the Siptar terrorist forces in this sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And one last document related to Izbica, 5D807 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, where is this leading, asking a witness who can't remember if something in a document says something?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you building up to some crescendo here?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has testified about his knowledge that after actions the terrorist forces would return to certain areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to explore that with respect to areas that are important to our indictment. I would hope that the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've certainly got loads of witnesses that have dealt with this already.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, we don't, Your Honour. As a matter of fact the commander of the 7th Infantry Brigade was never brought as a witness here, so this is the first witness I have that can address this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but your question --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Because the commander of the 7th Brigade is deceased, 7th Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but the questions are much more general than that, aren't they? They're not confined so far to a particular location.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, these questions have been specifically confined to the locations that have been in the combat orders, which is the region around Izbica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, well, this witness doesn't know about that area. He gave us a very general answer about no area that was not affected by terrorist fighting or terrorist presence and then anti-terrorist fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And since he doesn't have a statement, that's why I explored further to see if he knows of any of these actions, for which I have one more document for, that's a 5D -- 5D807. He is -- you will recall, based upon his position within the Pristina Corps, it's within his purview, it's within the items that he would be doing in the regular course of his duty, which is what I'm here to cross-examine him on, especially where it relates to things that might assist us in understanding the situation on the terrain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If I can give you your first question on this which is at page 8, line 18: "Would you agree with me that after an anti-terrorist action was completed it was often the case that the Albanian terrorist forces would very quickly return to that area and recommence with their terrorist activities?" And the answer was: "Yes, throughout the whole anti-terrorist fight against Siptar terrorist forces there was the spillover of the forces. After an action the territory would be left or it would be secured by a smaller force and then after a while it would be retaken again. This is just a system of joint vessels." Now, there you've got his answer in relation to the situation over the province, and you've had that answer from other witnesses. Now you're exploring a particular area that he doesn't know anything about, as I understand it, with documents which you can address us on in due course based on any other evidence that there is or has been or will be from people who know about these operations, and you've got loads of time to lead any evidence you wish to lead on that subject. So let's deal with things that this witness knows about, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, if Your Honour thinks I can lead evidence about military actions through police witnesses, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will now move on to action -- pardon me, to activities that were conducted jointly. Do you recall, sir, that the -- that among the activities of the military territorial detachments, the command group of the Pristina Corps for Djakovica proposed a plan for, among other things, organizing joint patrols in town with MUP forces to protect both stores and private residences from criminal activity? And while we're waiting for that we can bring up 6D750 to perhaps refresh your recollection of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you recollect this, Mr. Stefanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a document from the command post of the command group from Djakovica. I'm reading it now and I'm not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were you a member of the command group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, Your Honour, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, again we don't have any knowledge of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Until I ask, I can't find out, Your Honour. I believe that I'm conducting a fair and reasonable cross-examination of this witness that my client is entitled to under the Rules and the Statute. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On matters that you have a reasonable anticipation of this witness knowing about. We've had a witness, at least one and probably more than one, from the command group already.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And we had this witness testify about his knowledge of joint patrols in areas yesterday, Your Honour, which is why I posed the question to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Believe me, these questions are based upon testimony that this witness has made or I believe has knowledge of based upon the documents, my investigations, et cetera, and what other witnesses have said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is obviously my fault because I don't remember evidence of joint patrols yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe there was evidence of joint patrols. I don't have the transcript in front of me, but in any event, I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Joint patrols in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, in general, which is why I asked about Djakovica to see if he could confirm this. He talked about the good cooperation and the success in securing various municipalities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I have to express surprise that it didn't strike me yesterday, that piece of evidence, because it does seem very important and I'd be grateful for a transcript reference to that. Joint check-points, we've heard of constantly, but I have no recollection of joint patrols and I would imagine the Prosecution would be extremely interested in the concept of joint patrols as well. And I don't see anyone leaping up to tell me the transcript reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can't find it right now, Your Honour, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With regard to Djakovica, one more question or so about that and we'll move on. Do you recall that even after the conduct of an anti-terrorist action in the Reka or Caragoj valley that the concentration of terrorist forces in that region continued to be a threat to VJ and MUP units and that there was combat in that region between those elements, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning in Metohija the command post of the Pristina Corps and later the forward command post of the Pristina Corps - and this was something that was led by the Chief of Staff, Colonel Zivkovic - but I really have no more reliable information about what you're asking me than this. I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now if we can move on, you talked about the Pristina Corps being at 80 per cent, I believe was your term, of its manpower. Now, if we could have 6D1470 on the screen from the Pristina Corps's command dated 18 April 1999 on overview of replenishment and losses, and once that comes up on page 2 is what I -- I think the -- what the witness needs to be directed to, page 2 -- oops. I'll have to return to that, that's the wrong document. I have a different reference for that. Let's move on to see if you can assist me about 5D84 relating to check-points. This was a document I believe that was identified as being -- upon which you were going to be led but for which I don't recall any specific evidence in chief. Can you look in the section 5 which should be on the second page in Serbian and can you help me with who would have established the security regime within the zone of responsibility of the Pristina Corps and subordinated units for these check-points?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security organ of the Pristina Corps command with the brigade command. They set up check-points along roads in order to check anyone entering or leaving the area of responsibility of these brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And one last question about this: Were these -- can you tell or do you know whether these were mixed check-points or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were a number of those that were joint or mixed check-points, manned by both army members and the police and there were those that were manned separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Now I would like to ask you several questions related to resubordination, but first let me ask you one question -- or actually two questions about 1998. During the 1998 anti-terrorist actions involving the MUP and the VJ, were there significant problems in these actions because of the fact that there was no formal resubordination even foreseen at that time?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1998, as I said, I was the commander of the 52nd Mixed Artillery Brigade in the Milane garrison. I know nothing about 1998 in terms of what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Then in 1999 we have heard some indication that the true aim of the 1999 order on -- the April order on resubordination from the president of the FRY was to try and calm the stand-off between the republican police and the army in Montenegro. Do you recall anything about that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was discussed at a very high state level. I was back at the corps command and I certainly couldn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, when you do talk about resubordination of the MUP, what is your specific understanding of how this resubordination ought to have looked? That is to say, was it to be limited only to the act and duration of the combat actions?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order of the Supreme Command Staff and the 3rd Army command to the Pristina Corps command formulated a number of sentences that the MUP was being resubordinated to the army as a principle. At the beginning this created a number of problems in terms of implementation. We tried to talk to see what the best solution would be, but we failed. So it was back to square one for us. We could offer support, coordination, and cooperation. There is an order dated the 25th of April which tried to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stefanovic, the question is much more specific than that. The question is whether resubordination was meant to apply only when you were working together in combat or whether it was a much more general resubordination that was envisaged. Can you answer that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that order said full resubordination, without separating off certain parts of the unit or services or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was it your understanding that resubordination of the MUP was to include the secretariats of the interior, traffic police stations, OUPs, police stations, were they supposed to be subject to resubordination, as you understand that term to be applicable, in April 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's precisely what I was trying to explain. We at the corps command certainly understood that it was impossible to see this through as the order envisaged, and then a new document was drawn up by the corps command, if I remember well, on the 25th of April once the dead-line for resubordination had already lapsed. We tried to have the original order and put it into a more operational form by keeping the police unit alone involved and only when necessary as part of actions against the terrorist forces. The remaining services of the secretariat of the interior and the staff should keep on operating according to their laws and regulations. Therefore, we have this order and this order offers an overview of the situation. It would be a good idea probably to go back to that order and have a look if it's available.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You say it was impossible to see this through as the -- as envisaged. Do you know if certain military commanders continued to be confused or misled relying upon the initial order on resubordination, which you say was impossible to be implemented insofar as we've had several high-ranking military officers here to testify who have clearly testified that they believe resubordination was to apply even outside of combat actions?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're just talking about the first part, the first order, and I believe that we have to go back to the original order and the other order that puts the envisaged implementation from the original order into more operational form, and that is the only context that we can use to explain this, to look at this. An additional effort was made to interpret in a clearer fashion the whole thing and to make resubordination possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask a different question. Do you have any explanation for the fact that several high-ranking VJ officers have come into this courtroom and under oath testified that they believed resubordination applied even outside of combat actions? And do you concede that there was -- or do you concede that there was a problem still in getting this second more specific order understood by everybody out in the field?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This has to be observed on individual basis, whether anyone had the need to resubordinate the secretariat of the interior in their own zone; however, at the corps command and the army command most of the officers weren't thinking about that. That's why we had this new order defining exactly how this very important activity should be carried out. We defined its implementation in real-time, real-place terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Given that several officers of the VJ have testified here that they thought resubordination was supposed to be wider, do you concede the possibility that some of the complaints about resubordination that you heard stem from a misunderstanding of the legal limit and definition of resubordination under Article 17 of the Law of Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't put it that way. I would kindly ask you to be more specific and would you deal with this one thing after the other. We keep going around in circles in terms of the same story, but what I'm trying to say there is no understand [as interpreted] to have a different understanding in the corps command and in the army command in terms of the order from the 25th. There was a vacuum. We were area of the fact that there were problems ourselves. If individuals had aspirations to subordinate the SUP, the MUP, as a whole that is their personal idea, their own wish. But I'm saying that it was for the system to function in Kosovo and Metohija in terms of engaging the army on the one hand and the police on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Now perhaps you can clarify for me a bit your testimony involving the Drenica 1 action that you mentioned yesterday and at the beginning of today. Is it your testimony that one PJP unit actually refused to show up and refused to follow the army's plan for the action, whereas one PJP unit under Colonel Brakovic went along with the joint action?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The unit that was under Colonel Brakovic carried out the task throughout, whereas this unit that was there, the 122nd - I don't want to make a mistake - they did not accept to be subordinated to the 252nd Armoured Brigade. They wanted to act independently, along an independent axis, and that can be seen from these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, now you would agree with me, I hope, that there's a distinct difference between a unit refusing and not showing up and a unit showing up but not accepting the ordered tasks presented to them by the army; wouldn't you agree?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there certainly is a difference. Now we were talking about Drenica 1 that was planned on the 28th, and the beginning of the realization was supposed to be on the 1st of June. But we're talking about the 25th, that is just Drenica, without the number 1, the Drenica action. Then part of the forces of the MUP did not show up. Let us distinguish between the 25th and the 28th of May. These are two actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So is it your testimony that the MUP PJP unit refused to show up for the original Drenica action?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I've said, they didn't show up. I'm aware of that on the basis of the report of the brigade commander. It's not I, it's the corps command that knows that they did not show up and that the task could not be carried out, as had been defined and resolved through this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you attribute blame to the PJP for not showing up for that initial action, which then required Drenica 1 to be drafted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I'm not accusing anyone. I'm not saying that they are guilty or not guilty. They did not show up in accordance with the agreement and coordination to have this task carried out. The persons in charge in the police probably discussed the matter. I cannot talk about what the police are doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Before we move on with that, I have very specific -- concrete questions about that, not related to the police but related to the testimony of one of your colleagues. But first of all, we had testimony of Colonel Gergar last week that indeed he viewed resubordination to include that the units of the police were to be an integral part of his brigade even outside of combat operations. Would you agree with me that that position is not consistent with resubordination under Article 17 and, in fact, the order that came down for resubordination of the MUP to the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I have to repeat the question. It's my understanding that the translation was the exact opposite of what I said, that it was consistent.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, would you agree with me that Colonel Gergar, and in fact any senior VJ Pristina Corps officer who had testified that in fact resubordination of the MUP included resubordination of MUP units to his brigade outside of combat operations would not be in the spirit and letter of Article 17 of the Law on Defence and the order on resubordination?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, in your complex question there are six subquestions. Please let us deal with them one at a time. You keep asking me the same thing. I really do apologise, but this is the fourth time that I've been saying -- I'll repeat it if the Presiding Judge allows me to. There is the order, the first order, of the 25th, that it clearly defines this. Let us please look at the order of the 25th of April and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You may be having difficulty understanding the question; I appreciate that. But in the end of the day the question is: Does Article 17 of the Law on Defence allow for total resubordination or is it necessary to comply with that article that resubordination should be restricted to combat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, Article 17 of the mentioned Law on Defence speaks of resubordination, that resubordination can be carried out of all forces in the area of combat operations. It does not specifically define what is resubordinated and what is not resubordinated. That is why we had numerous problems and that is why I point this out, this order of the 25th of April. After agreement was reached, we wanted to see what it was that was being resubordinated and what remained within the scope of authority of the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The other part of the question was whether the actual order itself - and you can now elaborate on that - whether the actual order itself was not originally confined to combat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, precisely. That is to say it pertained to all, to the entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you say that the original order provided for resubordination not only in combat but in the entirety of the operations of the MUPs and SUPs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, precisely. If I remember correctly, I will try to paraphrase, I cannot quote it until I see it. All organs and units of the MUP should be resubordinated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me then that whichever officers would come here today and testify that this, all organs and units of the MUP would be resubordinated in toto, would you agree with me that they would be wrong?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's a matter for us to determine now in the light of the evidence, Mr. Ivetic. We've explored this sufficiently with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can return to the Drenica action, you mentioned the original action. If we could please have Exhibit P2014 on the screen. I believe you will find this to be the original Drenica order, and if we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could have the witness -- if I could have the usher's assistance to give the witness a hard copy, it might be easier or more efficient to work through these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First off, sir, are you familiar with this order; that is to say, did you draft it or are you aware of its drafting and the drafting of any map to go along with it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in the planning of this action?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. You can see my initials at the end, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did anyone with the MUP participate in the planning of this with you, of this particular action?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Not a single action was carried out off the cuff, so to speak. There was always coordination and working meetings that preceded it regarding the forces involved, the time of realization of the action in the combat against terrorist forces. This includes this one too.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it my understanding and your testimony that the -- for this action the MUP formations -- strike that. Is it my understanding -- is my understanding correct that your testimony is that the MUP personnel that engaged in planning with you planned the portion of this order and the tasks on the map that would have accompanied it for their units, for the MUP units?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a basic difference here between coordination and planning. I've been saying throughout, and let me say it now as well, this was coordination, work discussions and agreements on the engagement of the police forces on the one hand and the units of the army on the other hand. Planning is a different thing. After coordination one starts planning; everyone plans at his own level.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Is it your testimony that during the coordination with the MUP for this particular action, that the MUP personnel contributed the portion of this order dealing with the MUP units?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, coordinations are organized in order to find a solution that will create such positive conditions for carrying out the task that had been received. That is the essence of any coordination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is a much more specific question; I think you know it, Mr. Stefanovic. You're being asked what was the source of the planning of the tasks which are set out here for MUP units.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, at the coordination, agreement was reached with the representative of the police what the task was that the MUP could carry out and what the army could carry out; on the basis of that, the operative organ, or rather, the corps command created this decision and the decision map and all the other accompanying documents. I assume that the police command, or rather, of their -- the command of their unit did that at their own level. Then once one goes into the field, realization takes place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You see, I certainly am confused now by your answers because you initially told us that the MUP participated in planning, then you redefined that as coordination and said that the planning started after the coordination, but now you're saying the MUP would have had to plan the tasks before the coordination meeting. So you'll understand certainly my confusion at this stage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, not at a single moment did I say that planning preceded coordination. I do apologise if I misspoke. It is coordination first, invariably, and then planning follows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was this document referred to in the examination yesterday, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ah, right. So can we see what the tasks are then?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure. If we can look at the section --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, could you turn to the section giving tasks to the various units, I believe it should be on the second or third page of this order, although I don't have a hard copy in front of me anymore, relating to the MUP units and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it not paragraph 5 we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It ought to be, 4, 5, without seeing --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It indeed is the third page of the document, beginning at the top, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please can we go over the page, please. And the next page, and the next. So, Mr. Ivetic, is the only mention of the MUP in the first task?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is correct, and that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And it's just a very general statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'm about to tie it up with testimony from Colonel Mandic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, we've seen the assignments to units and if we can look at the beginning of that again, on page 3, the top of page 3, where the MUP units are mentioned. If in fact the MUP participated in this coordination in the manner that you identified, how do you explain the fact that the order doesn't even identify the specific MUP units that are supposed to take part by their numerical designation? Or is this a situation where the VJ prepared a plan for the police but not knowing the police structure was unable to identify the specific units that would take part in a task?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this order we can see the 252nd and the police unit and the JSO. We are certain that when this combat document was written the person from the police could not say which MUP units could be engaged. This happened several times because there was several actions, several tasks, several obligations, so one could not ensure invariably at the very outset what the exact number of the participating unit would be. We will see on the decision map that it is correct; namely, that it is defined on the decision map what unit this actually is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If the MUP personnel did not know what units they had available, how could they be the ones proposing an action for their units?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only problem here is in the numeration of the unit, not in the unit itself. Obviously they provided a unit, it's only the numerical identification that is a problem, what is the actual unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. And with the last page of the -- with the last page of the order we see that the 252nd Brigade, that is to say I think Colonel Mandic at the time, was supposed to be in charge of planning, organizing, and leading the action, that's in paragraph 14. Do you recall that being the case?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. I have the document, that's exactly the way it was. It was a smaller-scale action. As for the organs of the corps command, at that point in time they could not have known about the command of the 252nd and they couldn't have provided assistance. What was believed was that the command of the 252nd could prepare and carry out this action on its own, which indeed did happen several times. On the other hand, whenever the corps command could ensure a group of officers, they would always send them to subordinate units to provide assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you explain for us in the military sense the significance of the fact that it says the command of the 252nd Armoured Brigade will be in charge of the planning, organizing, and conducting of the combat operations. Does that, in fact, mean he will lead the overall action, the overall joint action which involves both MUP and VJ units?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the way this order regulates this. This was the 25th of May. What was still in force was the order on resubordination of the MUP, and it is on that basis that this task was spelled out. We really do know that in real life this did not actually happen --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this question --

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ultimately --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That being the case, if this operation, as you say, could not be carried out because of a MUP unit refusing to show up and, in fact, refusing to resubordinate, would you expect there to be a combat report written by Colonel Mandic explaining why he could not carry out this particular order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume -- well, I don't know, but I assume that the commander of the 252nd Brigade informed the corps commander because after that we started planning a new action, Drenica 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, Colonel Mandic indeed testified in these proceedings, and he identified the problem with this original Drenica action as being, first of all, that the order from the Pristina Corps command arrived too late for him to implement it and that his brigade was, in fact, not equipped and in a position to organize all the things and because of the fact that the order did not have the MUP units -- he didn't even know whom to contact and identified that he could not contact any of his neighbour forces, and that is why the action did not, in fact, become implemented. Are you willing to concede that, in fact, Colonel Mandic's testimony would be more appropriate or accurate to describe why the Drenica action did not proceed, the original Drenica action, so far as he was the officer on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have information from the interpretation booth that the interpreter did not understand the question. It's a rather lengthy question and perhaps there are some minor inaccuracies. I mean if our colleague Mr. Ivetic could rephrase it and put it in shorter terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's certainly clear enough in English, but if there is a difficulty it will need to be repeated, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll break it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware of the fact that Colonel Mandic testified that the order for Drenica came too late for him to implement it and that he was not equipped to communicate with any of the other forces that were to be involved in the action?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about Colonel Mandic's evidence; however, the order was made on the 25th of May, readiness by the 29th of May, that is a four-day period. Do you actually know when he received the order? He wasn't at the barracks at the time, he was on the ground in his own area. It wouldn't have taken him that much time to get himself organized. I can't accept this. Secondly, did he inform the corps commander of this? Did he inform anyone that he was unable to do this? I simply cannot accept this, what you are putting to me now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At page 20936 of the transcript, beginning at line 17, in discussing this order, Colonel Mandic said: "First of all, what I don't see defined here is which unit this is about. This is a very generic term. That is what I was unclear about. This is a very generic term as used in relation to police, as, for example, it said just VJ, whereas of course the VJ comprises a lot of smaller units. But the order arrived late, or rather, I received it late and I was unable to establish contact with these units. Therefore, I didn't even know which units would be operating on the task alongside the brigade." Is that something that you're hearing for the first time; and if so, do you concede now that perhaps there was another reason, that this was, in fact, the reason that the Drenica action could not be implemented?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I really can't accept that. There was a four-day period between the day the order was made and the dead-line. If we have anyone who will show when he actually received the order, perhaps then we can talk. That not being the case for the time being, four days would have been sufficient for him to get in touch with all the units that were envisaged. Apart from the PJP detachment nothing else is really defined here. There is the number of the unit that is supposed to get involved, there is the entire order for him, all the items are listed there, all the paragraphs of the order, so I can't accept this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry for the fact that you conflict with Colonel Mandic and his testimony, but that's what he said. Can you now concede that, in fact, you are mistaken about the reason --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: He's answered that question, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this a convenient time for us to break?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you got much longer?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think I should be able to handle it in about 20 minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stefanovic, we need to break at this stage. Could you leave the courtroom, please, with the usher, and we'll see you again at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, as you get seated I'd like to call up 6D712 as I have a few more questions about Drenica 1 before moving on to other topics of interest. And the question I have for you is perhaps something you can answer before the document comes up. Am I correct that upon planning the Drenica 1 action the Pristina Corps sent the written order -- sent the written order and a map with the assignments to all MUP units and formations that were to participate?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the order on my screen. No, no, it was sent to the MUP and they were supposed to inform their units. It wasn't sent to everyone. In the brackets you can see it says "to all units." This is by way of information, to all units, as it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You say "it was sent." Was the map also sent to the MUP with the placement and assignments of all the units participating in the action?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right now I can't remember whether it was or not, but certainly there should be a diagram containing the decision, like an excerpt, in relation to the MUP that was supposed to be sent along but I can't be positive about it right now and I can't tell you for sure whether it was sent or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You say there should be. Am I correct that it was the regular course and practice for actions in 1999 that excerpts of maps prepared by the VJ with positions and assignments of VJ MUP units was provided to the MUP by the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that wasn't the practice. It was decided on a case-to-case basis. This was the case perhaps several times because of the importance of a particular action or because of someone's inability to define coordination all the way, but to be quite specific, if such an excerpt from a decision by the Pristina Corps commander was received showing all the army units and all the MUP units, this part of the decision which we referred to as an excerpt can be used as a coordination plan - and please allow me - as a coordination plan. And this is then a basis for planning in relation to all the units that received these excerpts. When a brigade receives this, it's not yet a decision, it's just a basis on which they can then set up their own plans and decisions and orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to this Drenica 1 action that I believe you testified had problems because one of the MUP units didn't show up, would you, in fact, agree now -- or strike that. Would you -- knowing that Colonel Mandic, in fact, in his testimony identified the 122nd PJP as taking part and in paragraph 32 of his statement said that co-activity and good cooperation did exist between the two structures in the course of the execution of that particular action in spite of the claimed non-resubordination, would you, in fact, be willing to concede and revise your earlier testimony that there was a problem in conducting the action based upon the refusal of a MUP unit to show up?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that yesterday. Based on a report by the commander of the 252nd Armoured Brigade, the MUP unit did not show up and they could not start implementing the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's what I have a problem with, sir. You see, I have yet to see a combat report for this action that mentions in any way any problems with the functioning of the action as it relates to police participation; indeed for the record there are several I think that are in evidence or that are in the e-court system, 5D953, 5D234, 5D959, 5D1292, from various participants in the action, but I would like to turn to 5D235, which I think is the one that you ought to have the most familiarity with, it's the combat report of the Pristina Corps dated June the 2nd, 1999. And if we turn to page 4 of the same, and that's I believe in both versions if in fact we have an English translation. We may not have an English translation for that one. Can you please read out for me the section under section 6.1 that starts: "Commanders of the 3rd Army in the Pristina Corps were at the 52nd Motorised" --

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that. I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Page 4. I apologise, General. It's up on my screen. Page 4 and it's the section 6.1. Right there. Do you see, sir, in the middle of the screen the section that starts: "The commanders of the 3rd Army and Pristina Corps ..." Could you read that paragraph for us?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. "Commanders of the 3rd Army and the Pristina Corps state with the 52nd Mixed Artillery Brigade they checked certain issues and the situation turned out to be favourable. The corps command team is providing assistance to the 7th Infantry Brigade, the 37th Motorised Brigade, and the 252nd Armoured Brigade, and they are leading the actions at Drenica and Prekaze on crushing and destroying the remaining Siptar terrorist forces in the sectors of Mount Drenica and the sector north of Mount Cicavica."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First of all, sir, from this combat report I take it that you as part of this team from the Pristina Corps command was leading the entire action, Drenica 1; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I wasn't the one leading it. I was coordinating this on behalf of the Pristina Corps command together with a team that the corps commander had set up. I was not in command, to be quite precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the commanders of each of these specific units that were in command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I by all means want to be very clear and very specific. While the commanders of the various formations commanded their own formations, the team from the Pristina Corps command led the action, the Serbian word "rukovodili." Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they led, "rukovodili," which implies organisation, coordination, support, and cooperation; not, however, command. This is a functional relationship between various structures while carrying out a particular action.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And there were no MUP officers present leading the action with you, were there?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aside from the commanders of police units, there was no one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, ever author a combat report complaining about the inability to proceed with the tasks in this action due to lack of MUP resubordination or refusal to appear?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Several times I orally reported to the corps commander, each time I had been to one of the corps' units, but I never wrote down a report because I would see the corps commander every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That really doesn't answer the question. The question was: Did you ever report about the inability to proceed with the tasks in this action due to lack of MUP resubordination or refusal to appear? Now, does your answer refer to this action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, precisely this action, yes, because that's what we are talking about so that's what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So several times in relation to this action you reported on the failure of MUP units to appear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as I said yesterday, several days, more days, is how long this action took because of its importance and because of the huge responsibility entailed. We were facing a number of problems, as I said yesterday. Until the 252nd Armoured Brigade and the police unit finally dealt with that problem for each and everyone to get involved on a separate axis, and then the action went forward as planned in the decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll be moving from that action, so I don't know if Your Honours had any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Looking at P2809 briefly, sir, this is on engagement of MUP forces from the Pristina Corps command. Could you explain for me why the first paragraph relies upon the earlier order on resubordination and not the -- excuse me, relies on the earlier order from the 3rd Army on resubordination and not on the original Pristina Corps order on resubordination.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order by the 3rd Army command is a link to a new order. This could have been preceded by the corps command order that had been issued, but essentially it doesn't change a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at the Pristina Corps order, P1267, so you can have it in front of you for purposes of my question. And the question I have for you is: Are you aware of whether or not commanders of Pristina Corps brigades sent written orders to the MUP units or formations that were supposed to be resubordinated under them according to this Pristina Corps order that hopefully you will have in front of you shortly?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't quite remember right now whether a brigade command in writing requested for one of the police units to be resubordinated to it. All I know is about corps command orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Moving along then. If we can look at 5D1084, and if I could direct your attention to paragraph 6 on the first page where it discusses resubordination of territorial units of police. Can you explain for us what that term is supposed to mean?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a combat report of the 37th Motorised Brigade, their report to the corps commander that this unit had not resubordinated itself and that matters because it was in his area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the first paragraph under 2.1 of this document mentions some order Ovcarevo and Obrinje. Do you know if any PJP units participated in that anti-terrorist action?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say off the bat before I've looked at the order, at the document. There was so many actions that it's difficult to keep track of them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Would you turn -- let's turn to Exhibit 5D1085. We don't have the order but I believe we have the combat report, the post-combat report dated the 13th of May, 1999. And as we're waiting for this document to come up, sir, do you recall if on that date you were present at the command of the 37th Brigade and that you, along with the commander of that brigade and the commander of the 7th Infantry Brigade and members of the artillery group of the Pristina Corps and police from the 122nd PJP detailed the obligations and tasks of all participants in this action, Ovcarevo and Obrinje?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Based on this combat report I was at the time with the 37th Brigade, the 1st Corps artillery group. There was some coordination there, it was a work meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Now would you agree with me that your presence there was more for the purposes of coordinating the various VJ units rather than the police, who were not even within the zone of responsibility of the 37th Brigade and therefore could not be accused of failing to resubordinate to them?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. The main reason I went there were the corps units, the brigades; but this is the month of May already, and in that order you see that the police units were resubordinated. Perhaps I talked to them occasionally if -- but certainly there was no form of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can -- well, is it correct, sir, that the 122nd PJP that participated in this action was not within the zone of responsibility of the 37th Armoured Brigade, particularly in light of the fact that you testified several minutes ago -- or a while back that the 122nd Brigade was with the 252nd around this same time, participating in the Drenica actions?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about a 15-day period here, a fortnight. PJP units are quite mobile, they're police units used for manoeuvring, and they were involved all over Kosovo and Metohija depending on their mission at a given point in time. They did not have one particular area that they were assigned to and they weren't just staying in one area all the time, such as the army brigades. Therefore, no one should be surprised that police units are showing up in several different areas along with several different army brigades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ivetic, since you've had the extra time you were -- or the time after you indicated, are you about finished?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: About, yes, Your Honour, but I think I have about nine or ten questions left, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Please see how quickly you can now bring this to an end. There was at some stage in the last 20 minutes a prospect that we would finish the witness today, but it now is rapidly receding.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour, and to try and get rid of three questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, would you agree that to the end of your -- to the end of your answer to my previous question you could also add that the PJP units had, therefore, orders -- the same PJP unit would have orders from several brigades to resubordinate to them, that is, the same single PJP unit could have several brigades vying for resubordination?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way you formulated the question, it's practically impossible --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, hold on, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- if we go back to the order on the engagement of MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We're running out of time. Let's go to one of your documents to see how out of line I am. If we can look at 6D1023. This is attachment 2 to the Pristina Corps plan on engagement of its forces. Can you, looking at the -- let's go to the -- this is the part we want, isn't it? Would you agree with me, sir, looking at the second page of this exhibit, that the same PJP unit was supposed to be resubordinated to both the 354th Infantry Brigade as well as the 211th Brigade simultaneously for purposes of this engagement plan?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A unit cannot be resubordinated to several commands at the same time because if we look at the text we will see that PJP units will be used occasionally to execute actions in the fight against terrorist forces depending on the specific action and the agreements. So it's a planned activity, it is something that is planned and that is expected. It's not a specific action or a specific assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can go to 6D1460, that's the document I did not have before me before the break relating to replenishment and the Pristina Corps. And perhaps if I could have the usher's assistance to give a hard copy -- here we go, now it's up on the screen -- just give him a hard copy because then I can ask him to review it and cut it down to one question on this. Sir, you're going to be shown a document, and I'm simply asking you since you testified about the manpower and the mobilisation of the Pristina Corps, if, in fact, this official document from the Pristina Corps coincides with your recollection of the numerical strength, particularly the charts on the second, third page of this exhibit of the Pristina Corps at about the time listed, which is the end of April or -- mid-April or the end of April. I can't see the date on my screen.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is certainly an authentic report for that particular time, and we're talking about the 18th of April here.
